pr.title: When AsyncDrop impl is empty, sync drop generated in elaborator
pr.author: azhogin

issues.title: ICE: elaborate drop: index out of bounds
issues.body:

| ^ | | | expected one of `)`, `,`, `.`, `?`, or an operator | help: missing `,` warning: the feature `async_drop` is incomplete and may not be safe to use and/or cause compiler crashes --> code.rs:2:12 | 2 | #![feature(async_drop)] | ^^^^^^^^^^ | = note: see issue #126482 for more information = note: `#[warn(incomplete_features)]` on by default warning: type parameter `g` should have an upper camel case name --> code.rs:4:12 | 4 | async fn a(b: g, c: usize) {} | ^ help: convert the identifier to upper camel case: `G` | = note: `#[warn(non_camel_case_types)]` on by default warning: type `e` should have an upper camel case name --> code.rs:8:7 | 8 | union e { | ^ help: convert the identifier to upper camel case: `E` error[E0601]: `main` function not found in crate `code` --> code.rs:14:24 | 14 | impl AsyncDrop for e {} | ^ consider adding a `main` function to `code.rs` error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: `drop` --> code.rs:14:1 | 14 | impl AsyncDrop for e {} | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ missing `drop` in implementation | = help: implement the missing item: `async fn drop(self: Pin<&mut Self>) { todo!() }` warning: unused variable: `b` --> code.rs:4:15 | 4 | async fn a(b: g, c: usize) {} | ^ help: if this is intentional, prefix it with an underscore: `_b` | = note: `#[warn(unused_variables)]` on by default warning: unused variable: `c` --> code.rs:4:21 | 4 | async fn a(b: g, c: usize) {} | ^ help: if this is intentional, prefix it with an underscore: `_c` ```

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: use crate::elaborate_drop::{DropElaborator, DropFlagMode, DropStyle, Unwind, elaborate_drop};

TerminatorKind::Drop {
                        place,
                        target: succ,
                        unwind: unwind.into_action(),
                        replace: false,
                        drop: None,
                        async_fut: None,
                    }

The patch modifies `build_async_drop` in the drop elaborator used by the `ElaborateDrops` MirPass. It avoids an out-of-bounds access when an incomplete `AsyncDrop` impl has no `drop` item and emits a sync `Drop` terminator instead, which is drop-elaboration correctness rather than a query or generic analysis.

processing.reason:
The historical regression is a compiler ICE, not a defined program-level miscompilation. Before PR #141328, `build_async_drop` evaluated `tcx.associated_item_def_ids(drop_trait)[0]` for an incomplete `impl AsyncDrop for T {}`; because the associated-item list has length 0, rustc panicked with an index-out-of-bounds bounds check instead of later reporting E0046. The corrected code uses `nth(0)` and, if absent, emits a delayed bug plus a synchronous fallback `Drop` terminator.

There is no source-groundable pair of self-contained Rust functions that (a) preserves this exact historical transformation, (b) has identical signatures/harness/inputs, and (c) yields two different defined observable return values under Miri. A faithful "incorrect" model must either panic on the empty associated-item list, which is not a successful defined execution for `test_program_pair`, or use `get_unchecked(0)` on an empty slice, which is UB and likewise cannot satisfy the Miri/defined-execution requirement. Wrapping the indexing in `catch_unwind` or returning an invented sentinel would add arbitrary behavior not justified by the PR and is explicitly disallowed. On non-empty inputs both the original `[0]` and the corrected `nth(0)` select the same item, so no differential value exists there either. Therefore this compiler-recovery ICE cannot be encoded as the requested defined original/transformed value pair.

evidence: impl_item_refs may be empty if drop fn is not implemented in 'impl AsyncDrop for ...'

index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0
//~^ ERROR: not all trait items implemented, missing: `drop` [E0046]
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to assume the associated-item list is non-empty and index element 0 directly. For an incomplete `impl AsyncDrop for T {}` (no `drop` method), the list has length 0, so the elaborator panics with `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0` instead of letting normal trait checking report E0046. The corrected behavior replaces the raw index with `tcx.associated_item_def_ids(drop_trait).into_iter().nth(0).copied()`; when it is `None`, it emits a delayed bug and patches the terminator to a synchronous `TerminatorKind::Drop { place, target: succ, unwind: unwind.into_action(), replace: false, drop: None, async_fut: None }` and returns `pin_obj_bb`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source compiled with `#![feature(async_drop)]` (edition 2024) containing a type that implements `AsyncDrop` with an empty/incomplete impl, e.g. `impl AsyncDrop for HasIncompleteAsyncDrop {}`, where the type also has a `Drop` impl (or otherwise reaches drop elaboration / async-drop MIR shim construction). The two comparison programs should differ only in whether the `AsyncDrop` impl supplies the required `async fn drop(self: Pin<&mut Self>)`: the empty impl triggers the empty associated-item list; the complete impl yields a non-empty list.
analysis.originalLogic: In `build_async_drop` (drop elaborator used by the `ElaborateDrops` MirPass), the code unconditionally obtained the trait's drop function by indexing the associated item ids: `let drop_fn_def_id = tcx.associated_item_def_ids(drop_trait)[0];` and then built `Ty::new_fn_def(tcx, drop_fn_def_id, trait_args)`. This assumes the `AsyncDrop` trait impl always contains a `drop` item.
pitfalls: Do not assume trait associated-item lists are non-empty when building MIR shims: incomplete impls can be observed by drop elaboration before/alongside the E0046 error.
A delayed bug diagnostic should be paired with a valid fallback terminator; returning early without patching the terminator would leave the block malformed.
Using `async_fut: None` in the fallback keeps the terminator a synchronous `Drop`, consistent with drop elaboration's expected shape.
This is a defensive recovery path for erroneous input, not a change to correct async-drop semantics for complete impls.
preconditions: A local type implements `AsyncDrop` but omits the required `drop` item, producing an incomplete impl
The type is used in a context that causes drop elaboration / construction of async-drop MIR shims
Trait checking later reports E0046 for the missing item; the elaborator must not ICE before that diagnostic
analysis.summary: ElaborateDrops' async-drop elaborator indexed `associated_item_def_ids(drop_trait)[0]` unconditionally; when an `AsyncDrop` impl omits `drop`, the item list is empty and the compiler ICEs with an index-out-of-bounds panic. Fix checks `nth(0)` and, on absence, emits a delayed bug and patches a synchronous `Drop` terminator while still reporting the normal missing-item error.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI test under `tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/` (moved from `tests/crashes/140974.rs`) using `//@ edition: 2024`, `#![crate_type = "lib"]`, `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`, `#![feature(async_drop)]`, and an empty `impl AsyncDrop for HasIncompleteAsyncDrop {}`. Mark the impl with `//~^ ERROR: not all trait items implemented, missing: \`drop\` [E0046]` and provide a `.stderr` expecting only E0046 (no ICE). Run the test harness (UI/compiletest) to confirm the normal missing-item error is emitted and no index-out-of-bounds panic occurs. Do not claim actual execution here; this describes the intended test construction.
analysis.trigger: Drop elaboration calls `build_async_drop` for a type whose `AsyncDrop` impl has no `drop` trait item, so `tcx.associated_item_def_ids(drop_trait)` is empty and `[0]` panics.
